blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

technical_gate.canonical_finalizer_requirement: Exactly five distinct options A-E; one correct plus four distractors.
technical_gate.pre_correction_issue: Initial staged Q0604 contained five distractors (six total options) and was not eligible for PASS.

claim_audit.phenotype: NCBI Pseudohypoparathyroidism Evaluation supports hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, elevated PTH and exclusion of renal insufficiency; GeneReviews supports AHO with short stature, round facies and shortening of the fourth/fifth metacarpals.
claim_audit.correct_mechanism: NCBI Pathophysiology directly supports impaired PTH/PTHrP-Gsα-cAMP signal transduction and states that PTH1R activation normally stimulates Gsα and cAMP generation.
claim_audit.distractor_1: NCBI Hypoparathyroidism supports true PTH deficiency with low/inappropriately normal PTH, hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia; elevated PTH in the stem excludes this.
claim_audit.distractor_2: MedlinePlus GNAS/McCune-Albright sources support activating GNAS variants causing constitutive adenylyl cyclase signaling; this is the opposite signaling direction from GNAS-inactivation PHP.
claim_audit.distractor_3: MedlinePlus CASR supports activating CaSR variants causing excessive calcium sensing and suppression of PTH, inconsistent with elevated PTH.
claim_audit.distractor_4: MedlinePlus vitamin D-dependent rickets/CYP27B1 supports impaired calcitriol synthesis with low calcium and low phosphate; hyperphosphatemia in the stem argues against this mechanism.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hypocalcemia plus hyperphosphatemia indicates inadequate PTH effect. Elevated PTH establishes end-organ resistance rather than PTH deficiency. AHO skeletal features further support GNAS-related pseudohypoparathyroidism; the direct intracellular defect is reduced Gsα-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP signaling.
adversarial_second_pass.true_hypoparathyroidism_challenge: Would produce low or inappropriately normal PTH rather than the elevated PTH explicitly stated.
adversarial_second_pass.constitutive_gs_challenge: Constitutive Gsα/adenylyl cyclase activation is opposite to the impaired signaling required for PTH resistance and is linked to McCune-Albright physiology.
adversarial_second_pass.casr_challenge: Activating CaSR suppresses PTH secretion; it cannot explain elevated PTH.
adversarial_second_pass.cyp27b1_challenge: CYP27B1 deficiency can cause hypocalcemia with compensatory PTH elevation but typically lowers phosphate, conflicting with the hyperphosphatemia that PTH resistance explains.
adversarial_second_pass.renal_failure_challenge: Renal dysfunction can cause hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia and secondary PTH elevation, but the stem explicitly states normal renal function and includes AHO morphology.
adversarial_second_pass.hidden_assumption_check: No treatment threshold, numerical cutoff, dose, prevalence or unstated family history is required.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five options are mechanistic endocrine/signaling abnormalities of comparable grammatical form; the correct option is not uniquely specific by wording alone.
